finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is interpolated into the SQL string via an f-string. An unauthenticated attacker can break out of the LIKE clause and run UNION-based queries to read any table in shop.db, such as users or credentials. They can also read the products price and owner columns, which the endpoint doesn't otherwise return.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'")

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') takes the raw user input with no validation
term is formatted straight into the SQL text instead of being bound as a parameter
query results are returned to the caller as JSON, so UNION SELECT output is exfiltrated directly

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, escaping, or parameter binding on this path. No authentication or authorization decorators. The other two routes (lines 18 and 25) use ? placeholders, so only this route is affected. sqlite3 execute() rejects multiple statements, which rules out stacked queries but not UNION-based injection.

verdict.reason: app.py:11-13 takes request.args "q" and interpolates it into the SQL f-string at line 12 with no auth, validation or binding, then returns the rows as JSON at line 13, so UNION SELECT output is exfiltrated; the routes at lines 18 and 25 use ? placeholders as stated.

verdict_facts.reason: app.py:11-13 takes request.args 'q' and puts it into the f-string SQL at app.py:12 with no auth decorator, validation or binding, and returns the rows as JSON, so an anonymous UNION SELECT with two columns can read any table in shop.db.
